- **`styles/global.css`** imports the new module stylesheet.

Verified: `sheratan check` (no violations), `tsc` typecheck (clean), full test suite (26/26 passing), and live in headless Chromium against the running server at 127.0.0.1:54303 — 25 customer rows render correctly on the golden path, and simulating a failed fetch shows the error/retry UI with no rows or loading indicator present, with Retry successfully recovering the table.

Confirmed live: exactly 1 call for the initial refusal (immediate error, no rows/loader), and exactly 1 more call on Retry (list arrives, error clears).

It's done. The bug was the `resource()`'s built-in `retry: { attempts: 3, backoff: Exponential }`, which silently retried in the background before ever surfacing a failure — masking single refusals and letting one Retry click trigger up to three requests. I removed that automatic retry (the manual Retry button is the only thing that re-fetches now) and added a `retrying` state transition so a retry properly flips the view back to the loader instead of leaving stale error content showing. All three named tests pass, plus the full suite (28/28), `sheratan check`, and `tsc`, and I verified live against the running server: a single refusal shows the error with zero rows/loader, and clicking Retry makes exactly one more request and renders the table.
